At T=9/4, alpha=1/4, the equilibrium equation is a 27/40 contraction, locating the unique fixed point inside radius 12/13; the Jacobian row-sum bound 469/512 proves an explicitly invariant attraction square. Finite code separately verifies rational constants and numerical consistency. No unproved infinite conclusion depends on sampling.

value.rationale: The source treats the Euler step itself as an essential bifurcation parameter and shows bounded complex trajectories even for T>2, but cannot infer global state bounds from sampled orbits. An exact all-initial boundary at T=2 and its nontrivial neutral endpoint answer a natural question about the model. An attracting equilibrium plus open escape basin at T=9/4 gives a motivated qualitative coexistence not reducible to local fixed-point stability. The explicit outer radius, asymptotic escape direction/rate, and quantitative attracting square are useful invariant-phase-space data for interpreting discrete spiking trajectories; no unproved claims of chaos or full basin partition are made.
